title: Reconsidering Learning Objectives in Unbiased Recommendation: A Distribution Shift Perspective

problem.claim: Learning unbiased recommendation algorithms from biased feedback.

gap.claim: Existing unbiased recommendation methods have empirical success but generally lack theoretical guarantees, leaving gaps between theory and recent algorithms.

contributions.claim: Provides a theoretical understanding of why existing unbiased learning objectives work for unbiased recommendation.
Establishes a connection between unbiased recommendation and distribution shift, and develops two generalization bounds for existing unbiased learning methods.
Proposes Adversarial Self-Training (AST), a principled framework for unbiased recommendation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize their approach as addressing unbiased recommendation from a novel distribution shift perspective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world and semi-synthetic datasets show that AST is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies learning unbiased recommendation algorithms from biased feedback.
Existing techniques have advanced empirical performance, but most lack theoretical guarantees.
The paper explains existing objectives through distribution shift and derives generalization bounds.
The paper introduces Adversarial Self-Training for unbiased recommendation.
Experiments on real-world and semi-synthetic datasets report AST effectiveness.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the assumptions or formal statements of the two generalization bounds.
The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not describe the architecture or optimization procedure of AST.
